questions.explain: Wait analysis is the mandatory first step: SOS_SCHEDULER_SLEEP dominating with signal_wait_pct > 25% indicates real CPU pressure. PAGEIO waits = storage bottleneck; LCK_/lock waits = contention; THREADPOOL = connection/pooling problem — none of which are fixed by adding vCPUs.
options: High CPU always means the instance is too small — scale up immediately
Run wait event analysis first: SOS_SCHEDULER with signal_wait > 25% = real CPU pressure; PAGEIO = storage problem; LCK_ = contention; THREADPOOL = pooling problem
Check the storage size and double it
Restart the instance and see if it recovers

questions.explain: Each step up the r6i ladder exactly doubles compute cost; moving from db.r6g.2xlarge ($0.960/hr) to db.r6g.4xlarge ($1.920/hr) adds roughly $8,410/year. The chapter's point: a two-week query optimization (~$7,700 of developer time) pays for itself in under 13 months versus a $9,000/year scale-up.
options: Scaling is nearly free; cost is not a factor
One tier doubles performance for only 10% more cost
Downsizing is the only option that changes cost

questions.explain: The remediation sequence: 1) update statistics, 2) add missing indexes (online on Enterprise), 3) fix memory grants (update statistics first; targeted MIN_GRANT_PERCENT hints), 4) connection pooling discipline, 5) rewrite pathological queries. Scaling stays on the table but is deferred until the optimization ceiling is reached.
options: Update statistics → add missing indexes → fix memory grants → tighten connection pooling → rewrite pathological queries; defer scaling until the optimization ceiling is reached
Scale up first, then optimize if time permits
Only add indexes; other steps don't matter
Rewrite the application from scratch

questions.explain: Three high-impact parameters: max server memory (cap it, leaving 10–15% for OS plus connection overhead — not default unlimited), MAXDOP (1 or 4 for OLTP when CXPACKET dominates), and cost threshold for parallelism (raise the 1990s default of 5 to 40–60 for OLTP). These deliver measurable CPU reduction with zero infrastructure cost.
options: Increase all timeouts and retry counts
Set MAXDOP to 0 and cost threshold to 1
Cap max server memory (leave headroom for OS), set MAXDOP appropriately (1–4 for OLTP), and raise cost threshold for parallelism from 5 to 40–60
Enable every trace flag available
questions.q: Which parameter-tuning changes should be evaluated before finalizing a scaling decision?

questions.explain: Scaling is approved only after all optimization steps, with guardrails: CPU > 75% sustained over 7 days after query optimization and buffer/cache hit rate < 95%, plus latency > 2x baseline and connections > 85% of user_connections after pooling. Every scaling event gets a documented Decision Record and a 30-day review (scheduled before the incident closes) with downgrade criteria: CPU < 40%, cache hit > 95%, connections < 60% of max.
options: A single CPU spike above 90% is sufficient
CPU > 75% sustained over 7 days after optimization AND buffer/cache hit rate < 95% (with other thresholds); document a Decision Record and schedule a 30-day review with explicit downgrade criteria
Management approval alone
Any time query latency exceeds 100ms once
